annotation.title_clean: Using generative AI and large language models
annotation.title_en: Using generative AI and large language models
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora
annotation.venue: Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora website
annotation.summary_en: Health NZ guidance on staff use of generative AI and LLMs. It recommends caution, bans entering patient or confidential data into unapproved tools and using them for clinical decisions, requires checking and acknowledging AI-generated content, and outlines risks: privacy, inaccuracy, bias, opacity, Māori data sovereignty, language gaps and IP.
key_provisions_or_claims: Staff and contractors must not enter personal, confidential or sensitive information into unapproved LLMs
Generative AI must not be used for clinical decisions or personalised patient advice
Users must take full responsibility for checking outputs and acknowledge AI use
Plans to use generative AI require advice via the expert advisory group process
Risks identified include privacy breaches, bias, hallucination, lack of transparency, Māori data sovereignty, and IP
